<div class="sphinxpress-doc">
<section id="concepts">
<h1>Concepts</h1>
<section id="git-first">
<h2>Git-first</h2>
<p>Releaseledger is git-first. Git tags and commit ranges define the shipped change
set. The canonical evidence of what shipped is <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">git</span> <span class="pre">rev-list</span> <span class="pre">--reverse</span> <span class="pre">--topo-order</span> <span class="pre">&lt;base&gt;..&lt;head&gt;</span></code>
— every commit reachable from the release target and absent from the previous release.</p>
<p>Taskledger, issue trackers, and PR descriptions are optional provenance that enrich
curated entries, but releaseledger works correctly with only git.</p>
</section>
<section id="source-refs">
<h2>Source refs</h2>
<p>A source ref is a coverage identity. Two kinds are accepted:</p>
<ul class="simple">
<li><p><strong>Global refs</strong> (taskledger, GitHub, etc.): <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">tl:task-0006</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">github:pr-42</span></code>.
Canonicalized by ledgercore.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Git commit refs</strong>: <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">git:&lt;7-to-40</span> <span class="pre">hex</span> <span class="pre">sha&gt;</span></code>. The primary evidence type for
git-first workflows.</p></li>
</ul>
<p>A <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">git-range:*</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">git-tag:*</span></code>, or <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">git-branch:*</span></code> ref is a non-coverable
range marker — useful as release metadata but never creating a missing-coverage row.</p>
</section>
<section id="release">
<h2>Release</h2>
<p>A release is a versioned record stored as <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">release.md</span></code> with YAML front matter
and an optional Markdown body. It tracks status, previous version, release date,
source boundary, source refs, and changelog file metadata.</p>
<p>Release statuses are:</p>
<ul class="simple">
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">planned</span></code></p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">draft</span></code></p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">candidate</span></code></p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">released</span></code></p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">yanked</span></code></p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">canceled</span></code></p></li>
</ul>
<p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">canceled</span></code> means the release was never shipped: it is excluded from
previous-version inference and not built into public changelogs by default.
Canceled releases may carry <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cancel_reason</span></code> and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">superseded_by</span></code> metadata
and remain visible in <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">release</span> <span class="pre">list</span></code> as an audit tombstone.</p>
</section>
<section id="entry">
<h2>Entry</h2>
<p>An entry is one release-note item stored under
<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">releases/&lt;version&gt;/entries/entry-NNNN.md</span></code>. Entries are grouped by kind for
changelog rendering.</p>
<p>Entry kinds are:</p>
<ul class="simple">
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">added</span></code></p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">changed</span></code></p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">fixed</span></code></p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">removed</span></code></p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">deprecated</span></code></p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">security</span></code></p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">docs</span></code></p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">quality</span></code></p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">internal</span></code></p></li>
</ul>
<p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">documentation</span></code> and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">doc</span></code> are accepted aliases for <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">docs</span></code>.</p>
<p>Entry statuses are <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">draft</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">accepted</span></code>, and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">rejected</span></code>. Changelog builds
include accepted entries by default.</p>
</section>
<section id="event">
<h2>Event</h2>
<p>Events are append-only operation rows. They do not store wall-clock timestamps
or before/after deltas. Releaseledger relies on git history for chronological
review and on per-record revisions for validation.</p>
</section>
<section id="commit-audit-sheet">
<h2>Commit audit sheet</h2>
<p>A commit audit sheet is a per-release review artifact that maps every commit
in the selected git range to a reviewer decision and, when applicable, to a
release entry. It is evidence state, not changelog prose.</p>
<p>The sheet exists to prevent release notes from being generated from commit
subjects. Each row records the commit SHA, inspected paths,
reviewer-observed behavior, public/internal impact, decision, and target
release entry. Public changelog entries are written from reviewed behavior,
API/docs impact, changed paths, tests, and diff evidence. Commit subjects are
evidence-only and must not be copied or mechanically transformed into
release summaries.</p>
<p>Decisions are <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">needs_review</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">accepted</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">grouped</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">internal</span></code>, and
<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">rejected</span></code>. Strict release review fails when rows remain uninspected, when
public rows lack accepted entry coverage, or when an entry summary matches a
commit subject.</p>
<p>This concept keeps Git as the canonical source of shipped changes while making
the human or agent review work durable and auditable.</p>
</section>
<section id="versioning">
<h2>Versioning</h2>
<p>Release and entry files contain <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">versioning.schema_version</span></code> and a positive
<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">versioning.revision</span></code>. New records start at revision 1, and the revision
increases by exactly one whenever that record file meaningfully changes.</p>
</section>
<section id="index">
<h2>Index</h2>
<p>Releaseledger rebuilds <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">indexes/releases.json</span></code> and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">indexes/entries.json</span></code>
after mutations. Indexes are derived state and should remain deterministic.</p>
</section>
<section id="global-refs">
<h2>Global refs</h2>
<p>External provenance is recorded as caller-supplied global refs, for example
<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">tl:task-0103</span></code>. Releaseledger stores these refs but does not resolve or
validate external ledger state.</p>
</section>
</section>
